description:
THE BLOCKER, design doc section 2.3. src/app_scaffold/mod.rs:149:

  pub fn spawn_physics_thread<T, F>(state: SharedState<T>, mut step: F) -> JoinHandle<()> {
      thread::spawn(move || loop { step(&state); })
  }

Two defects: thread::spawn compiles for wasm and PANICS at run time; and the
loop lives inside the thread, so the physics owns its own cadence and cannot be
scheduled by anyone -- not Rayon, not a Web Worker, not a test harness.

Replace with a bounded tick() the platform layer drives. This is the core of the
epic and everything else waits on it.
title: Replace spawn_physics_thread with a bounded tick() driven by the platform layer

description:
FOUND 2026-09-10 while building the GROUPR golden-tape comparison (tests/groupr_u238_gendf_golden.rs, session_01AhE6XBx3nRd81aHLQrciQe). Same input (ENDF/B-VIII.0 U-238, MAT 9237, err = 0.001, 293.6 K), NJOY2016 ac5adf5 vs the crate:

  NJOY RECONR: 448,168 points in the final unionized grid ("points affected by resonance integral check = 363092")
  NJOY BROADR (errthn = 0.001): points in = 448,168, points out = 155,207
  crate RECONR + BROADR: 961,139 points (BROADR keeps every point)

Two separate upstream behaviours the port does not have:

1. RECONR resonance-integral relaxation (reconr.f90:105-117, 425-430). Upstream reads err, tempr, errmax, errint; errmax defaults to 10*err (1 %) and errint to err/20000 (5e-8 b). Where a grid point's contribution to the resonance integral is below errint, the convergence test uses errmax instead of err. Effect: negligible cross sections (sub-threshold U-238 fission, ~2.5e-7 b, is the measured example) are converged only to ~1 % and far fewer points are added. The crate refines every reaction to err, which is the tighter answer but 2.1x the points. Consequence already visible: the golden test's tier 2 has MT=18 1.1e-2 off NJOY for exactly this reason (asserted at 3e-2 with the explanation; MT 1/2/102 are within 9.2e-4). Port the errmax/errint pair as ReconrConfig fields with upstream's defaults so the grids (and timings: the crate's U-238 RECONR takes ~150 s in release) match.

2. BROADR thinning (broadr.f90, the errthn/thnmax cards; grep "thin" in src/broadr/ finds no thinning at all). Upstream thins the broadened grid back to the errthn tolerance (448k -> 155k here); the crate returns the whole input grid broadened. A 6x denser PENDF is not wrong, only slow for every downstream consumer (GROUPR flux tabulation, ACE tables). Port the thinning pass (with the same thnmax bound that 31fa3880 added for the broadening itself).

Both are grid-size/performance parity items, not correctness defects: the golden test shows the crate's values are the more converged ones. Validate any port against the two point counts above and re-run tests/groupr_u238_gendf_golden.rs (tier 2 MT=18 should then move from 1.1e-2 toward tier 1's 2e-6).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: 2026-09-10: item 2 (BROADR thinning) is now covered — broadn ported (op-tubm): U-238 961k -> 133k points below thnmax vs NJOY 448k -> 155k. Item 1 (RECONR errmax/errint relaxation) still open; the measured 8-9e-3 capture deviations at tens of keV in tests/broadr_light_nuclide_pendf_golden.rs are NJOY's 1% errmax chords on ~1e-5 b cross sections, consistent with this bead.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: 2026-09-10 wave 4: item 1 (errmax/errint) is now PORTED as part of the op-yr43 fix -- RefineTolerances::defaults(err) = {errmax: max(10 err, err), errint: err/20000} (reconr.f90:428-430), applied exactly as resxs does (reconr.f90:2398-2412). No ReconrConfig fields yet (defaults only; add overrides when a deck needs them). U-238 point-count effect (961k -> ?) not yet measured this session -- run examples/endf_to_broadened_xs.rs and note it here. New parity item observed: the crate keeps per-MT grids (Si-30: 7,184 for MT=1/2 vs 5,011 for MT=102) where NJOY unionises all MTs onto one 7,284-point grid; lin-lin values agree, only the point sets differ.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: 2026-09-10 wave 4: MEASURED after the errmax/errint port: examples/endf_to_broadened_xs.rs (fixed -- it asserted identical 293/900 K grids, which broadn's adaptive insertion broke) reports U-238 broadened MT=1 = 103,244 points (wave 3 after broadn: 133k; NJOY BROADR: 155,207). The crate now has FEWER points than NJOY; note the per-MT (non-unionised) grids and that the 0 K RECONR count was not captured by the example (NJOY 448,168). GROUPR golden tier-2 MT=18 residual re-measured by the full suite (see session report).

title: njoy RECONR/BROADR grid parity: port errmax/errint resonance-integral relaxation + BROADR thinning (961k vs NJOY 155k points on U-238)
